cohort: The study included 232 term pregnant women undergoing caesarean sections, categorized into two groups based on their abdominal circumference.
finding: Women with a larger abdominal circumference (AC > 109 cm) undergoing caesarean sections under spinal anaesthesia experienced a significantly higher rate of hypotension, more pronounced hemodynamic changes, higher spinal anaesthesia levels, and required more ephedrine compared to those with a smaller AC (AC < 95 cm).
